lines.title: What does routing actually save you? Here's a day of agentic coding through the router: five long agent sessions in Claude Code, and the quick questions in between.
lines.local: The quick questions and small edits stayed on this machine. They're free, and they don't touch your Claude limits.
lines.subscription: The agent sessions are where the tokens go: every step resends the whole conversation. On your Claude subscription, that's worth this much at API prices.
lines.paid: Then the session limit hit. Instead of stopping, the last two sessions moved to a paid API. That's the only money actually spent today.
lines.saved: Compared with running the whole day on a frontier model through its API, this is what routing saved. And the overview keeps a running total for the week.
lines.end: Semantic Router dot net. Spend frontier money only where it counts. It's open source, and MIT licensed.

local: 16 quick questions answered on this machine: a local model, free, no Claude limits used.
subscription: $18.59 of Claude use, at API prices: 3 agent sessions, 250 requests, 24M tokens in the day, included in your subscription.
paid: $0.73 actually spent: 2 agent sessions after Claude's session limit, on paid-api-deepseek-chat-v3, 73 requests.
saved: $42.14 saved: $42.86 if all 339 requests went to Opus through its API, minus $0.73 spent (Usage:ReferenceModel).
The Overview, this week: 339 prompts routed, 5% served locally (16), $42.14 saved against claude-opus-api, $0.7256 spent, $18.59 of subscription use at API prices.
